transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… mostly my sleep. I’m barely sleeping in a way that feels useful anymore. I lie there going over client models in my head, and then I’m up at 3 or 4 with my stomach tight. By the time I go to work, it feels like I never really rested.
Do you find that you're worrying about something specific when you wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning?
Usually work. Client models, assumptions, things I might’ve missed… it just starts running in my head. Then I wake up around 3 or 4 with my stomach tight, and I don’t really get back to useful sleep.
Did something specific happen at work that started these sleep problems?
Yes… I think so. It really started after the merger, when they reorganized our Caribbean-market division. That was about three years ago. Since then it’s just sort of… stayed.
Are you worried about things other than work when you wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning?

Mostly work. I mean… when I’m awake like that, it’s usually the client models replaying in my head, things I might’ve missed. I can’t say it never drifts, but that’s the main thing. Then I’m just lying there with my stomach tight, and by morning it feels like I didn’t really sleep.
Did something upsetting or traumatic happen to you around the time of the merger at work?
Not… traumatic, no. At least I wouldn’t call it that. It was upsetting in the work sense—stressful, a lot changed—but nothing like a specific incident I can point to.
Is the stress you feel about work present throughout the day, or is it mostly at night when you're trying to sleep?

It’s mostly when I’m trying to sleep, or when I wake up too early. During the day I can keep moving, focus on the work. But at night I’ll lie there replaying the client models, and then I’m up at 3 or 4 with my stomach tight… and I go in feeling like I didn’t really rest.
Do you feel anxious or on edge during the day, not just when you're thinking about work or trying to sleep?
I don’t know… not really in a clear way. I can feel tense sometimes, but I haven’t paid much attention unless it’s tied to work or when I’m trying to sleep.
Do you feel anxious when you're doing things you enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends and family?
I’m not sure. I don’t really do much that I’d call hobbies lately. With family or friends… I guess I can feel kind of tense, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s anxiety.
Do you feel anxious when you're with family or friends, even if you're not thinking about work?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’m sitting there feeling anxious, exactly… but I may not notice it unless someone points it out.
Do you feel anxious when you're doing everyday activities, like shopping or watching TV?
I don’t really know. With things like shopping or TV, I’m mostly just… doing them. I haven’t noticed feeling anxious, but I’m not sure I’d always recognize it.
Do you feel anxious when you're by yourself, not doing anything in particular?
I’m not sure. When I’m by myself, I’m usually just sitting there or trying to get through the time. I don’t really know if I’d call it anxiety.
Do you feel anxious when you are not thinking about work?
I don’t really know. If I’m not thinking about work, I don’t notice anxiety exactly… it’s more like I’m just there. Hard to say.
Do you feel anxious when you are engaged in an activity that you normally find relaxing?
I’m not really sure. If it’s something that’s supposed to be relaxing, I don’t notice anxiety so much… I just don’t feel very settled, I guess. But I don’t know.
Do you feel anxious when you are on vacation or completely disconnected from work?
I don’t really take vacations much, so… I’m not sure. If I’m disconnected from work, I don’t know that I’d call it anxious. It’s just hard to tell.
Do you feel anxious when you are with family or friends and not discussing work?
I’m not sure. With family or friends, I’m usually not talking about work, but I don’t really pay attention to whether I’m anxious. I guess I just feel kind of… distant, maybe. Hard to say.
Do you feel anxious when you are thinking about something pleasant?
I don’t know. I don’t really notice anxiety with pleasant thoughts… sometimes it just doesn’t feel that pleasant, I guess. Hard to explain.
Do you feel anxious when you're thinking about something that has nothing to do with work?
I’m not sure. I don’t really track it that way. If it’s not about work, I might still feel… uneasy, but I don’t know if I’d call it anxious.
Do you feel anxious when you are thinking about something that brings you happiness?
I don’t really know. I don’t pay attention to it that closely… and honestly, things that should make me happy don’t always feel that clear to me. So I can’t say for sure.
Do you feel anxious when you are thinking about something that has nothing to do with work or your daily responsibilities?
I’m not really sure. I guess even when it’s not work or responsibilities, I can still feel kind of unsettled, but I don’t know if that’s anxiety exactly.
Do you feel anxious when you are not thinking about anything in particular?
I don’t really know. If I’m not thinking about anything specific, I might still feel… not exactly calm, but I don’t know if that’s anxiety.
